title: SIU ends probe: [North York Mirror Edition]
article: The Special Investigations Unit has cleared a Toronto Police officer in the death of a 26-year-old man in June.
O'brien Christopher-Reid was shot following a confrontation with the police on a footpath in Wilket Creek Park June 13.

As part of the SIU investigation, investigators measured, mapped and obtained aerial photographs of Edwards Gardens and Wilket Creek Park, seized three police firearms and the spent cartridges and projectiles and interviewed a total of 29 police and civilian witnesses.
According to the SIU, police received a call at about 12:10 p.m. about a shirtless man who was walking with a knife in the area of Lawrence Avenue near Edwards Gardens.

Three officers arrived in the parking lot of Edwards Gardens and were directed by witnesses to where Christopher-Reid was last seen. About 10 minutes later, two officers saw him near a bridge holding an extension cord. According to the SIU, the officers told Christopher-Reid to get down on the ground and one officer grabbed hold of his elbow. Christopher-Reid broke free and an officer pepper sprayed him as he ran past.
Police followed Christopher-Reid for about 100 metres before he came to a sudden stop and pulled a knife from his pants. Police ordered him to drop his weapon.

According to the SIU, Christopher-Reid held the knife above his head and moved toward the three officers who were about 20 to 30 feet away. The officers backed away on the path and repeatedly shouted at the man to drop the knife.

The report said Christopher-Reid continued to advance on the officers and yelled either, "We're all going to die" or "You're all going to die." He then turned with the knife raised above his head and moved toward one of the officers, who was off the path and backed up against some bushes and trees. All three officers fired at Christopher-Reid.
A total of eight shots were fired from the officers, four of which struck Christopher-Reid. He was hit three times in the back and once in the left side of his chest.
One officer was also shot in the leg, receiving a superficial wound.
